points.text: A technique for finding faint objects by starting at a bright, recognisable star pattern and moving in steps using nearby stars until the target is reached.

questions.question: Q: How can you estimate angular separation without equipment?

points.text: Using hand measurements at arm's length: little finger ≈ 1°, three middle fingers ≈ 5°, fist ≈ 10°, outstretched hand span ≈ 20°.

questions.question: Q: What factors affect seeing conditions?

points.text: Atmospheric turbulence (causing twinkling/scintillation), light pollution, cloud cover, humidity and air transparency.

questions.question: Q: How does a planisphere work?

points.text: It has a rotating disc with an oval window; you align the date and time to see which constellations are above the horizon at that moment for your latitude.

questions.question: Q: What is the difference between a transit and an occultation?

points.text: A transit is when a smaller body passes in front of a larger one (e.g. Mercury across the Sun). An occultation is when a larger body completely hides a smaller one (e.g. the Moon occulting a star).
